source.citation: Unattributed drawing of a log building on a shore, with a woman in its doorway, a crowd of children on the bank, canoes afloat and drawn up, and a white lighthouse tower on a low point in the middle distance. Deposited by the repository owner on 2026-09-03 with the description "a great pic of the shore along there and the eliza chappel school at clark and lake". Taken from a 2018 Digital Research Library of Illinois History Journal post on Chappell (drloih_chappell), where it is the first image, uncredited: a republication.
what_it_does_not_supply: its own subject - whether the log building it draws is the Sauganash's annex or another schoolhouse is unsettled, and T-0649 established that the lighthouse cannot settle it
its own date, artist, title or original repository: the 2018 journal post it was taken from (drloih_chappell) credits none of them

its caption: "the eliza chappel school at clark and lake" is the deposit's paraphrase of the 2018 post's own caption ("roughly at Lake and Clark Streets are today"), which places the school where it moved in 1834 and was written by the post's compiler, not the artist, so the drawing's subject is still the open fork the note below describes
any coordinate, footprint outline or dimension
a station: the drawn figure scale falls off with depth 1.523x short of what a single viewpoint demands, so no drawn position on the sheet can be inverted to a viewpoint
a height for the tower: its foot is not drawn, and the admissible band is 4.65 to 23.41 m
corroboration of the Braunhold engraving: nothing has yet been read off it
what_it_supplies: nothing yet: no attribute of any committed record rests on this image
